gift.title: Opening: the winter trip of the day
gift.text: Torun is an old town of red brick where the air smells of gingerbread and mulled wine simmers on the market square. A route for one winter day: from the Town Hall to the Gingerbread Museum.

task.text: Open the first door and your streak has begun. Come back tomorrow: the next one opens at midnight.

gift.title: Hidden places of Belarus
gift.text: The places catalog has spots that tour buses never reach: manor houses, lakeside lighthouses, abandoned churches. Start with a selection of places on the map.

task.text: Add three routes to "I want to go" — this is your winter wish list.

gift.title: Riddle: guess the town
gift.text: A town with a Radziwill family palace and a UNESCO-listed park. In winter the ponds freeze over and the palace is reflected in the snow.

task.text: Name this town.

questions.question: Which town in Belarus is known for the Radziwiłł palace and park ensemble, a UNESCO World Heritage Site?

gift.title: An author's story about winter
gift.text: MeTravel authors share how they travel in winter: short days, frost, empty castles with no lines. Read the community's articles and pick your favorite authors.

task.text: Follow an author whose route you liked — their new trips will show up in your feed.

gift.title: Winter idea roulette
gift.text: When you don't know where to go for the weekend, let chance decide: the roulette picks a route from the catalog.

task.text: Spin the roulette and save the route you like to "I want to go".

gift.title: Kalyady: fact of the day
gift.text: Kalyady, the Belarusian Christmastide, runs from Christmas to Epiphany. Carolers go from house to house with a star on a pole, singing and wishing the hosts well, and in the village of Semezhevo near Kopyl the UNESCO-listed "Kalyady Tsars" rite takes place.

task.text: Quiz: three questions about Kalyady.

questions.question: On which day of January do Orthodox Christians in Belarus celebrate Christmas?
Which symbol is carried on a pole at the head of a Kalyady procession?
What is the name of the UNESCO-listed Kalyady rite from the village of Semezhevo?

gift.title: Christmas markets of Poland
gift.text: Krakow, Wroclaw, Katowice, Gdansk, Poznan, Warsaw: dates, addresses and tips on when to go so you don't have to wait in line for oplatek wafers and mulled wine.

task.text: Choose a market and mark the trip with the "I'm planning" status and a date.

gift.title: Winter quest in Grodno
gift.text: The "Christmas and New Year" quest in Grodno: the old town, castles above the Neman River and the Christmas tree on the square. It takes two hours on foot, with hints on your phone.

task.text: Complete the first step of a winter quest in your city.

gift.title: Where is this? Map
gift.text: A 16th-century castle in a small town in the Grodno region, a UNESCO World Heritage Site: five towers, an inner courtyard and a pond that turns into an ice rink in winter.

task.text: Tap the map where this castle stands. A hit within a 5 km radius counts.

gift.title: Where to go for a winter weekend
gift.text: Weekend routes around Belarus: one day, no overnight stay, with a warm cafe at the end. Search by region and distance from home.

task.text: Find a route for the coming weekend and open its page.

gift.text: Winter photos by travelers: snow-covered churches, frozen lakes, the lights of Christmas markets. The best shots of December will receive a rare award from the team.

task.text: Upload your winter photo to a new trip or note.

gift.title: Traveler profile
gift.text: A completed profile is your travel book: countries, cities, badges and rank. Other travelers use it to find travel companions.

task.text: Complete your profile to 100%: name, photo, about you.

gift.title: How to thank authors
gift.text: A peer award is a badge one traveler gives another for a helpful route. The author sees who thanked them and for what.

task.text: Give a badge to the author of a route that helped you.

gift.title: Polish winter quests
gift.text: Krakow, Wroclaw, Gdansk and fifteen more Polish cities — Christmas quests through old towns with markets and nativity scenes.

task.text: Open a city landing page and save the quest route.

gift.title: Riddle: guess the place
gift.text: The largest lake in Belarus: 80 square kilometers of water, a pine-covered shore and health resorts where winter is quieter than anywhere else.

gift.title: Memory book
gift.text: You can turn your MeTravel trips into a PDF book: photos, routes and notes. In December the book is free — a gift for yourself or your loved ones.

task.text: Build a PDF book from your trips.

gift.title: Group trips
gift.text: Travelers are looking for companions for winter trips: from one-day outings to New Year tours. Browse the plans or create your own.

task.text: Apply to join a group trip or create a plan.

gift.title: The article you never finished
gift.text: Many of us have a trip sitting in drafts that we never got around to telling about. December is the time to finish it: readers are looking for winter ideas right now.

task.text: Publish a draft or start a new article.

gift.title: Winter routes of Belarus
gift.text: In winter all the castles and museums in Belarus are open, and the roads to them are cleared first. Mir, Nesvizh, Lida, Novogrudok — the classic two-day winter loop.

task.text: Mark five trips with the "Was" status — they will appear in your travel calendar.

gift.title: The longest night
gift.text: December 21 is the winter solstice: Minsk gets about seven hours of daylight. The best time for evening routes with illuminations: town halls, castles and Christmas markets are at their most beautiful after sunset.

task.text: Quiz: three questions about the longest night.

questions.question: Roughly how many hours of daylight does Minsk get on December 21?
What is the name of the astronomical event when the night is the longest of the year?
In which country is Reykjavik, the northernmost capital of Europe?

gift.title: Story of the year
gift.text: Which trip of 2026 do you remember most? A short note — three paragraphs and one photo — will become part of the community's "Year in Review".

task.text: Write a short note "My trip of 2026".

gift.text: Your 2026 in numbers: the countries and cities you visited, trips, quests and badges.

gift.text: Merry Christmas! MeTravel winter art — a card to share with the people you want to travel with in the new year.

gift.title: New Year: a wish
gift.text: May 2027 bring more roads than plans, and more plans than excuses. Put together a wish list for the year — at least three places.

gift.title: Kalyady: the secret door
gift.text: Merry Christmas! Kalyady continues until Epiphany: on these days people in Belarusian villages still walk with the star. Thank you for being with us all December.

task.text: A secret door: it opens only on its own day.
